_about: What the remake's role table calls a hazard but the original does not.
The port reads the remake's entity_roles.json for its roles, and that table is the
remake's design decision rather than the converter's. In one place it is wrong about
the original: enemy_killer sits under `hazard` beside death_area.ent, destroyier.ent
and lava, all of which kill the player on contact.
436701..437083) is 69 instructions, and instruction 7 jumps to the return when
isMinion(other) is false - so a player, a crate or a thrown stone touching it gets
nothing at all. It is sensor=0 and the converter gives it a solid StaticBody2D, which
is a floor the player can stand on, and it lies below the bounds of 44 levels across
worlds 3 and 4. Left in the hazards it would kill the player on contact in every one.
It is not dropped, only moved: sim/Minions.hpp owns it, where destroying a minion is
what it is for. No chapter-2 level places one, so nothing that passes today changes.

_source: THE LEVEL'S OWN EDGE, which is the death nothing in this port tested for: a player
who walked off a ledge fell for ever, and the owner found it by jumping into a pit.
GameStateController::checkGameLost (assets/GameStateController.angelscript, bytes
123759..125310) holds two deaths, not one. Instructions 0..116 are the hp death;
instructions 117..184 are this one, and read exactly:
charPos = character.GetPositionXY()
if (charPos.x > maxPos.x || charPos.y > maxPos.y ||
charPos.x < minPos.x || charPos.y < minPos.y)
Past that, and only when !gameFinished, it logs GAME_CHARACTER_DIED_BY_FALLING,
plays playDieByFallSound(), Hide()s the character, drops a skull.ent marker at the
screen edge and calls finishGame(true) - which sets gameLost and is what makes
checkGameEnd raise the levelLostLayer a delay later.
maxPos and minPos come from the constructor (bytes 121296..122160, instructions
size   = g_scale.scale(vector2(32, 48))
maxPos = SeekEntity('max').GetPositionXY() + size * 2
minPos = size * -2
THE MARGIN IS size * 2 ON BOTH ENDS, and reading it as a bare `size` on the max end
was a misread of the disassembly worth recording. Instructions 77..80 compute
`size * 2` into a variable and instruction 81 is `VAR v8`, which pushes that
variable's INDEX; instruction 96 is `GETREF`, whose operand is a STACK OFFSET and
not a variable index, so the listing's `GETREF v2[size]` annotation names the wrong
variable. `size * 2` has no other consumer in the function, and a compiler does not
emit a multiply it never reads - so instruction 96 resolves to it. The result is
symmetric with the minPos line, which is what a reader would expect anyway.
`size` is scaled by g_scale for the original's screen. The port's level pixels are
the converter's unscaled units - level1's `max` node sits at (512, 256) in a level
512 x 256 px - so in this space the scale is the identity and the margin is (64, 96).
The `max` entity is the same node the port already reads as level_bounds for the
camera clamp (Camera.hpp) and the beholder's spike cull (boss.json). Every one of the
128 levels places one.
